title: Feature-flagged rollout controls for overload protection (per region/model) + safe defaults
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (ENG-4821), we need a deterministic, safe way to roll out overload protection by region and model without requiring redeploys. This PR adds feature-flagged rollout controls (per region/model, with optional tier scoping) and safe default configuration behavior across the request path (gateway -> routing -> runtime). Goal is to enable canarying in us-east for 1–2 models (ENG-4834), while keeping global defaults conservative and preventing accidental broad enablement. What’s included: (1) Rollout config schema + validation: Introduces an overload_protection.rollout config document with allowlisted regions/models, optional tier filter (hosted tiers only for now), and an explicit enabled boolean. Validation is strict: unknown regions/models rejected; empty allowlist is treated as disabled. (2) Evaluation library shared by gateway + routing: Adds a small internal package to evaluate whether overload protection should be active for a request based on (region, model, tier, endpoint type). This avoids drift between layers and makes error semantics consistent. (3) Safe defaults / fail-closed behavior: If config is missing/invalid/unparseable, overload protection remains disabled (i.e., we do NOT start shedding due to config issues). If protection is enabled but the downstream breaker service is unavailable, the gateway will not shed based on breaker state (it will fall back to current behavior), but will emit a metric to surface the gap. (4) Admin toggle for emergency mitigation: Adds an admin-only override to disable overload protection for a region (INT-1182). This is intended as an incident lever and is audited + time-bounded (auto-expires after 2h unless renewed). (5) Observability hooks: Emits metrics for rollout evaluation decisions and config load status to support canary monitoring and alerting (pairs with ENG-4829/ENG-4830). Out of scope: The actual breaker logic/state machine (PR #18457) and gateway admission control middleware behavior (PR #18421). This PR only provides rollout controls and safe defaults around them. Rollout plan: Start with enabled=false everywhere; push config enabling us-east + model=rw/open-llama-13b and rw/mistral-7b-instruct for internal traffic only; validate metrics/dashboards; then widen to production tiers in us-east before additional regions/models. Testing: Unit tests for schema validation + matcher evaluation; integration test that config reload propagates to gateway without restart; audit log assertions for admin override create/update/expire. Checklist: [x] Backward compatible defaults [x] Admin override audited [x] Metrics documented in code comments [x] Oncall runbook note added (follow-up in ENG-4828) [x] Added guardrails to prevent enabling wildcard “*” for models/regions (must be explicit).
commits: config: add overload protection rollout schema + validation
gateway: wire rollout evaluator into overload middleware init (no behavior change when disabled)
routing: expose rollout evaluator + plumb into breaker client construction
admin: add emergency disable override with TTL + audit logging
obs: add metrics for config load status + rollout match decisions
tests: unit + integration coverage for config reload and overrides
docs: add inline guidance and examples for rollout config
review_conversation: Mina Haddad: Can we guarantee this won’t accidentally enable shedding globally if the config is malformed? I want the default to be “off” unless we explicitly say “on”. Benji Okafor (author): Yep—implemented fail-safe defaults: missing/invalid config => rollout disabled; also disallow wildcards for region/model to force explicit allowlisting. Added tests for parse failures and unknown region/model strings. Rafael Mendes: For incident response, we need a simple kill switch that doesn’t require editing the main config and waiting for propagation. Also: please ensure it’s audited and time-bounded so we don’t forget it’s on. Benji Okafor: Added admin override with TTL (2h default), stored in routing admin store, and emits audit events on create/update/expire. Gateway reads the override via routing on its normal refresh cycle; we also emit a metric when override is active. Linked INT-1182. Amara Diallo: In the gateway path, please avoid adding a dependency that can block request handling. If routing is down, I don’t want config fetch to become a new failure mode. Benji Okafor: Acknowledged. Gateway uses local config snapshot and does not synchronously call routing for rollout decisions. The only routing interaction is via existing breaker client paths; if routing is unreachable we emit a metric and fall back to current behavior (no shedding due to breaker state). Jordan Lee: We should explicitly scope to hosted tiers only for now, and ensure that tier parsing is stable across OpenAI-compat endpoints. Benji Okafor: Added tier scoping as optional config filter; default is “any hosted tier”. Dedicated is not affected in this PR. Also added a small normalization helper shared with gateway error/compat code. Allison Grant: Please keep metric labels bounded—no raw model IDs as labels if there are many. Use a model_class or a small allowlist label. Benji Okafor: Updated metrics to use model_group (curated enum) and region; full model name is included only in structured logs/traces, not as a metric label. Added a cardinality note in code. Connor O'Brien: Release-wise, can we ensure this is completely inert without config changes? Benji Okafor: Confirmed; enabled defaults to false, and matcher requires explicit allowlist entries. Added a canary config example to internal docs comments and referenced ENG-4834 rollout plan. Status: Changes requested addressed; approvals from Rafael, Mina, Amara, Jordan. Merged via squash after CI green.
release_notes: Internal: adds per-region/per-model rollout controls for overload protection with safe defaults and an audited, TTL-based admin override. No customer-visible behavior change until enabled via config.
